description:
Comment “REWIRE” and I’ll drop my book link.

How to stop getting in your own way by not worrying about the end goal:

1. Stop worrying how far you have to go.
Every time you look at the finish line, you’re reminding your brain of everything it hasn’t done yet. Instead, use it as inspiration by acknowledging that the enjoyment is in the journey.

2. Everyday identify the next small action only.
Not the plan. Not the five year vision. The one thing you can do today. Your brain builds new pathways through repetition of small actions, not through thinking about big ones. One action, done consistently, is how identity actually changes.

3. Repeat it until it’s automatic.
This is where most people give up, right before the repetition becomes a pattern. Change doesn’t feel like change while it’s happening. It feels boring. It feels slow. But your brain is rewiring beneath the surface every single time you show up.

Put one foot in front of the other. Just focus on the next step. That’s when everything changes.

#rewireyourbrain #neuroscience #changeyourlife #neuroplasticity
transcript: The number one thing that's stopping you from becoming who you want to be is how much you emphasize the end goal. And as somebody who has studied neuroplasticity, I can tell you that this shows up in three different ways. Number one is worrying about how long it's going to take. Number two is worrying that it's too late. And number three, worrying that the goal is so big that it feels unattainable. All three keep your brain focused on the gap, and your brain perceives that gap as a threat. Therefore, cortisol rises, motivation drops, and all of a sudden you've stopped before you even started when you learn that the brain only cares about repetition you learn to put one foot in front of the other day in and day out and just focus on the next step instead of the end goal that is when your entire life changes
